requiredFindings.title: Bind capture to the custody judgment instead of taking a new baseline
requiredFindings.finding: Selection retains only File after judge_project_object returns (), discarding the sample that passed custody. capture_carrier later takes an entirely new metadata baseline; carrier_sample extracts metadata without applying the custody predicate. If the selected opensip.json is rewritten or made others-writable after selection but before this new baseline, both capture samples and the later same_carrier recheck can equal the changed state. The admission therefore accepts bytes or custody that differ from the selection judgment. Local capture has the same judgment-to-new-baseline gap. Retaining the same descriptor prevents replacement from redirecting that descriptor, but does not prevent mutation of its object.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Retain the full sample associated with the successful custody judgment alongside the descriptor on the analysis path. Require the capture samples to match that judged sample, with appropriate custody/name checks, and keep the legacy path's charges unchanged. Add deterministic controls interposing a rewrite and a custody change between selection/judgment and the read; require refusal rather than accepting the new baseline. Retain the post-capture replacement controls.
evidence: examine returns Examined::Config(Option<File>) without a judgment sample
capture_carrier compares only samples acquired after the original judgment
same_carrier compares against that later metadata baseline
X2 r9 item 3a; MB item 2 swapped-file/race control; plan r3 section 1.1

requiredFindings.title: Judge and retain parents of optional absence observations
requiredFindings.finding: first_absent opens each existing prefix but never calls judge_directory, named, or the installation filesystem admission. If I/host exists with wrong private custody and settings.json is absent, capture_optional returns Ok(None). Only the string host/settings.json is retained. recheck_absent opens those prefixes again without custody, exact-name, filesystem or original-identity checks, so replacement or a custody change of the parent also passes while the leaf remains absent. Neither the session's required files nor its captured-file list receives that optional parent. Native open_child_directory explicitly proves none of those custody facts. This is not a positive absence under a judged parent as LD-B1B-2 requires.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Observe optional absence through the same charged private-directory, exact-name, filesystem and attachment judgments used by capture. Retain the judged existing parent chain and the first absent component, then recheck those original owners and the absence under the held fence. Preserve full-recheck/latching semantics on refusals. Add controls for a wrong-custody existing host directory with an absent leaf, custody changes, parent replacement/detachment, absent host appearing, and leaf appearance.
evidence: first_absent retains Vec<RetainedDirectory> only locally and drops it on return
State.absent is Vec<String>; recheck_absent reopens names and accepts vanished prefixes

requiredFindings.title: Make the exception pin enforce actual variable names and test confinement
requiredFindings.finding: The permitted checker passes on the current bytes, but it does not enforce two claimed invariants. EXPECTED pins tokens HELPER_INPUT, x8c::HELPER and MARKER rather than their constant values; changing the corresponding definitions to a different environment name leaves the scan unchanged, while the enclosing Clippy allow still permits the new read. Test confinement is computed as any line after the first cfg(test) module opener (or merely a _tests.rs filename), without tracking the module's closing brace or whether an included file is actually test-gated. Moving an already-allowed function into production after such a module would still be classified test-only. These defeat the promised exact law list and sole production exception.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Resolve or explicitly pin the three constant-backed environment names, and verify actual enclosing cfg/test-target scope rather than a first-line threshold or filename suffix. Check item-level allowance attachment within that scope. Add focused negative controls that change a constant's value and move an allowed test helper outside its test module; both must be rejected without relying on Clippy to detect an already-allowed method.
evidence: CALL records call.group(2) unchanged; EXPECTED contains constant identifiers
test_from is a single line index and test_only uses index > test_from
M3-B r5 item 9 requires a concrete exact exception list confined to test targets
plan r3 section 1.5 promises checks by file, enclosing item and variable name

requiredFindings.title: Complete the accepted plan's behavioral controls
requiredFindings.finding: The order test drops a successful CarrierAdmission and calls that a refused pack; it neither exercises a refused project-layer pack nor asserts absence of registry capture, RESERVED rows, leases and journals. The legacy ledger test compares two executions of the candidate (small versus large carrier and absent versus present local), not the base-computed expectation required by plan r3, and does not cover both wrapper paths. The CI tests check outcomes rather than the promised counting observer, so an ignored local lookup need not fail. Finally the split hostile-environment controls compare carrier hashes and only resolvedConfigDigest plus provenance layer names; they do not compare the complete resolved record/provenance (operational values are excluded from that digest). The clean children inherit the parent environment instead of using the planned cleared baseline, and no new separate permitted-Git-refusal assertion is present. LD-B1B-4 avoids a public facade appropriately but does not retain the same control coverage as claimed.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Supply an observable refused-project-pack composition control with the required no-registry/no-effect assertions, matched base ledger expectations for the legacy read-session and write-gate wrappers, and a local-lookup counting control. Keep the crate split, but compare complete stable resolution/provenance output including operational fields, use a controlled clean child environment, and separately assert the permitted Git environment refusal. Add the judgment-to-read and optional-parent controls required by RF-01/RF-02. Update evidence and SCOPE.md to describe what the controls actually establish.
